subject: function signatures, match/promotion logic, & user defined functions

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: function signatures, match/promotion logic, & user defined functions
parts:
I committed some code for declaring function
type signatures. It's in a helper-include file:

src/stan/gm/function_signatures.hpp

It declares the type of all of Stan's built-in
functions. It doesn't include the basic
binary and unary arithmetic operators, which
are handled in a different branch of the grammar.

As written now, you can't use the arithmetic
operators (i.e., +, -, *, /) for vectors or
matrices. I could change that later pretty easily.

In order to add a new function to Stan,
a declaration of its type needs to go in the above
file (or the appropriate method called before the
parser is called if you're running programatically).

The function itself needs to be defined for
both doubles and stan::agrad::var inputs in arbitrary
positions. The simplest way is to fully template
(diff template variable for each argument with a computed
result type). It's more efficient to override
and define the partial evaluations for the auto-difs
as we do for all the built-ins so far.

When compiling a Stan model file, I check that there's
a unique function. In the end, I went through and
did the int to double promotion properly. So if you
declare two functions:

double foo(int x, double y);
double foo(double x, int y);

and try to call foo(2,3), you'll get an error, as
both are equally good promotion candidates, requiring
one int to be promoted to a double. There aren't any functions
that have this kind of pathological signature set in the
built-ins, but who knows what users might do.

Eventually, to make Stan extensible with user-defined
C++ functions, I'll need to have a way to include user
headers and declare the type of new functions. I'm
thinking something like the following to include a function
foo() mapping a double and vector to a double.

extensions {
using my::functions; // include in generated code

include <foo/bar/baz.hpp> // carry over to model includes

function double f(double,vector); // type info
}

I'm NOT going to do this for the first release, though.
It'll be easy enough to extend the language later in
a backward-compatible fashion.

- Bob
